Subject: Infrastructure assessment for EU oncology pilot

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the intro — we spoke briefly at the conference and OncoVate is ready to pilot an LLM assistant for clinicians that will process limited PHI (patient IDs, treatment notes) in the EU. Before we lock timelines, procurement needs a clear comparison: private (air-gapped/VPC) deployment vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs) for a compliant, low-latency pilot.

Specific asks:
- A short bulleted comparison of security controls (KMS/HSM, audit logs, network isolation).
- Sizing recommendations for an initial pilot (target: 50 concurrent clinical sessions, ~15 QPS peak, p95 token latency <250ms).
- Rough monthly cost band (order-of-magnitude is fine), and lead times for on-prem or VPC private delivery vs reserved dedicated capacity.

We have a small procurement packet attached for context. Can you share a one-pager and a technical note by EOD next week?

Best,
Lena
Dr. Lena Berger
CTO, OncoVate

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Infrastructure assessment for EU oncology pilot

Thanks Lena — appreciate the detail. High-level answers below and we'll follow up with a concise tech note and a sizing spreadsheet.

Quick bullets:
- Security controls: Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) gives you full network isolation + customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit log retention in your environment. Dedicated (reserved) is logically isolated with encrypted disks, customer keys via Redwood KMS integrations, and audit export — but control plane still runs in our managed region.
- Sizing: For 15 QPS peak and 50 concurrent clinical sessions we typically recommend a small reserved cluster (~4 x A100-80GB equivalent) with KV/prefix caching to hit p95 <250ms. Private deployments often need an additional 25-40% capacity buffer for batch/maintenance windows depending on on-prem networking.
- Costs & lead times: Rough bands — Dedicated reserved: ~€25k–€45k / month (depends on commitment & model quantization). Private: higher upfront (setup & network compliance) — one-time onboarding + infra procurement; monthly OPEX ~€40k–€70k. Lead time: Dedicated reserved (2–4 weeks); Private VPC (4–8 weeks); on-prem (8–14 weeks) depending on procurement.

Questions for your team to refine numbers:
1) Expected average input tokens per request and max sequence length?
2) Any hard retention / audit window >90 days?
3) Is HSM required on day 1 or negotiable to a later milestone?

I'll loop in Marissa with a sizing workbook and a short one-pager.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Sales, Redwood Inference

Sofia / Karthik — drafting sizing notes and attaching traffic estimates. Initial assumptions made in the spreadsheet; please review and adjust the capacity scenarios below before I send to OncoVate: 

Attachments included: onco-traffic-estimates.csv, compliance-eu-checklist.pdf

Draft capacity scenarios (alpha):
- Scenario A (Dedicated reserved, baseline): 4 x A100-80GB nodes (8 GPU instances w/ continuous batching), autoscale + burst to 6 nodes. Prefers quantized 8-bit model for cost parity. Expected sustained QPS 10–20, p95 target ~220ms with prefix caching.
- Scenario B (Private VPC, hardened): 6 x A100-80GB dedicated nodes (air-gapped option requires additional control plane connectivity work); reserve NICs for low latency, HSM integration for key custody. Plan for 30% headroom for on-prem variability.
- Scenario C (Pilot minimal): 2 x A100 + 1 smaller instance for routing & caching (good for functional validation; not production-grade).

Operational notes:
- For PHI we recommend strict rollback/testing windows and a canary route to Dedicated if Private onboarding slips.
- Attach audit retention requirements to the contract (90/180/365 days) — affects storage and cost.

Can Karthik confirm node counts and a quick op-ex vs cap-ex sketch? I have a short one-pager ready once we align.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Marissa — my technical notes and quick cost sketch below. Quoted earlier traffic file for numbers.

Quoted assumptions: average request 1,200 tokens in+out, peak concurrency 50 sessions, 15 QPS peak, retention 180 days for audit artifacts. Model: open-tuned LLM, quantizable to 8-bit with minimal quality loss.

Private (VPC / on-prem) — Hardened config (recommended if they require full custody):
- Baseline infra: 6 x A100-80GB (GPU count ~48), dedicated control-plane proxy nodes, HSM cluster for KMS, separate logging cluster for audit retention.
- HA and maintenance: N+1 redundancy (requires +1 node spare).
- Latency: p95 ~180–240ms with aggressive KV caching and local routing.
- Security: Customer-managed KMS, network ACLs, optional air-gap (adds procurement complexity).
- Cost: CAPEX heavy if on-prem (hardware + rack + networking), OPEX approximate: €45k–€68k / month (includes monitoring, patching). Lead time: 8–14 weeks.

Dedicated (Redwood reserved) — Managed but isolated pool:
- Baseline infra: 4 x A100-80GB reserved, autoscale buffer to 6 for bursts. Shared control plane with per-customer isolation and dedicated tenancy flags.
- Latency: p95 ~200–260ms under same assumptions.
- Security: Customer key integration supported (bring-your-own-key via Redwood KMS connector), full audit export to customer storage.
- Cost: OPEX ~€28k–€42k / month depending on commitment & model tuning. Lead time: 2–4 weeks.

Operational tradeoffs and recommendation:
- If OncoVate needs absolute custody (HSM on day 1 & air-gapped), go Private — higher cost and lead time but clear control.
- If timeline and lower TCO are priorities while still meeting EU data residency and strong audit controls, start with Dedicated reserved with a documented migration path to Private in the contract (canary and fallback policies).

Action items for the packet:
- I will prepare a two-page tech note with: exact node lists, expected token throughput numbers by route, and an ops checklist for onboarding.
- Marissa: finalize the one-pager with the three scenarios and cost bands.
- Sofia: propose 30–45 minute follow-up call next week with OncoVate + procurement — they asked for a procurement path.

— Karthik
